title: Backcasting from 'Whistleblower/Incident Signals Are Aggregated': A Mini Sentiment-and-Theme Tracker for Lab-Safety Discourse

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting from 'Whistleblower/Incident Signals Are Aggregated': A Mini Sentiment-and-Theme Tracker for Lab-Safety Discourse

**Problem:** A success state where governance gets early warning of safety problems requires aggregating diffuse public signals (researcher posts, departures, leaks). Today these signals are scattered; there's no lightweight tracker surfacing emerging safety-concern themes around specific labs.

**Direction:** Collect a public corpus of safety-relevant discourse (e.g., public posts/news about a few labs over a time window) and build a simple theme-and-stance tracker: cluster topics, tag whether each item raises a safety concern, and chart concern-volume per lab over time. Use basic NLP (embeddings + clustering + LLM-coded stance with a fixed rubric). Validate clusters by hand.

**Why it matters:** Backcasting from 'early-warning governance' shows signal-aggregation as the precondition for an NTSB-style proactive function. A working prototype tracker demonstrates how diffuse public discourse can be turned into governance-relevant early warning. Public text only, runs on a consumer GPU; squarely an outsider infrastructure prototype.

**Relevant context:** The Future Society NTSB-analogue agenda; AI Incident Database community reporting; CSET harm taxonomy for tagging. Open Problems in Technical AI Governance on monitoring and early-warning capacities.
